leads.summary: A valid duplicate touchpad name ending in -1 is not paired with its mouse node
leads.consequence: Hyprland v0.56.2 appends -1, -2, etc. to colliding input names. The hardware helper can select a name such as msft0001:00-093a:0255-touchpad-1, but related_devices only accepts a terminal -touchpad/-trackpad. Even when a corresponding mouse node is present, off disables and saves only the chosen touchpad, emits a successful Touchpad disabled OSD, and reload disables only that saved primary. The emulation node stays enabled; on does not repair the missed sibling. This is conditional on a paired mouse node and a duplicate primary name, not proof of any particular machine's topology. Derive association from physical device identity or account for Hyprland collision suffixes without arbitrarily disabling an unrelated -mouse node.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral follow-up to Opus (opus/followup-1.md): unchanged since base, needs a second identically named device, R1 already covered; dropped

leads.summary: Coordinate the multi-digitizer touchscreen PR when integrating this shared toggler
leads.consequence: Related open PR #11835 changes the touchscreen hardware helper to emit all digitizers, one per line. This head reads that output as one device string and rejects its embedded newline in require_device. Off then exits 1 without any eval or saved file (touchscreens remain enabled); on tries any previously saved names, removes the file, then exits 1 with Invalid touchscreen device name before the new names. Git three-way merge of #11835's own diff with this head has four conflict hunks in the toggler and two in the Lua reader, so this is an integration warning, not a claim the merge already produced a broken artifact. Merge the multiple-primary array handling and this PR's per-touchpad sibling discovery and saved-name ordering; retain both fixture sets.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator git merge-file (coord/) 4+2 conflict hunks, Opus re-confirmed; published as Related PR note

leads.summary: Changed enable tests do not assert saved and rediscovered names are applied once
leads.consequence: A plausible regression that drops seen[$name]=1 in enable still passes the complete changed test. When saved names overlap the live helper's names, such a regression sends duplicate hyprctl eval calls for each overlapping name, increasing IPC and potentially obscuring partial failures in a presence-only log; the pinned implementation itself does maintain seen and does not have this behavior. Count exact eval lines for the off/on and saved-query cases, including no duplicate primary or mouse sibling.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (observation 4); idempotent effect; not published
